locations.name: Scene Restaurant & Lounge
locations.description: Sit-down restaurant and lounge at Bridge Street Town Centre attached to the Cinemark theater, framed by reviewers as a mall dining stop that also works before a movie rather than an in-theater dining concept. Reviewers specifically call out sushi, street-corn dip, elote flatbread, pork nachos, and a fried-chicken sandwich; the restaurant is described as quiet, with booths and tables. Recent food quality is mixed — a strong dinner report sits next to a complaint about cold marinara and lackluster nachos.

locations.name: Studio Eats Lancaster
locations.description: Food-and-beverage counter inside Cinemark Lancaster IMAX and SCREENX, with reviewers describing pizzas around $12, loaded bacon-cheese fries, and free refills on large drinks. A small arcade sits alongside. Recent reviews are polarized: a first-timer called the food unexpectedly good, another described a $50 order dispute that escalated with the assistant manager to the point of being asked to leave.

locations.name: Reserve Kitchen & Bar - Playa Vista
locations.description: Cinemark's Reserve concept at Playa Vista, positioned as the theater's higher-end kitchen-and-bar. Only a handful of reviews carry text; the strongest calls it 'the best restaurant and bar in Playa Vista' and singles out cook and staff pride. Not enough reviewer signal to grade seating or service model.

locations.name: Movie Bistro - Rialto Renaissance Marketplace
locations.parking_notes: Reviewers note the parking lot fills up on opening weekends for major releases.
locations.description: Cinemark Bistro at the Renaissance Marketplace, run on an in-seat delivery model reviewers describe in detail — order from the Cinemark app and food (burgers, fries, wings, wraps, salads including a Southwest that gets repeat praise) is brought to your seat with no need to speak to anyone. Full bar. Large reclining lounge chairs with cupholders and elevated footrests; the IMAX house is called out for an especially wide screen. Reviewers mention wheelchair-accessible dining and 'The Box' motion-seat auditorium. Parking gets crowded on opening weekends.

locations.name: Studio Eats Roseville Galleria Mall
locations.parking_notes: Mall parking garage; reviewers report it fills up during peak times and suggest arriving early.
locations.description: Food-and-beverage program inside Cinemark Roseville at the Galleria Mall, with reviewers describing mobile ordering that delivers popcorn, snacks, and drinks to reclining seats. A dedicated bar serves beer, wine, and hard alcohol that reviewers say can be carried into the theater. Multiple recent reviews single out staff friendliness by name. Parking in the mall garage can be tight on peak days; some reviewers park at the adjacent Pinnacle at Galleria and walk over.

locations.name: Studio Eats Carefree Circle
locations.description: Studio Eats concessions inside Cinemark Carefree Circle XD and IMAX, a large multi-wing theater. Reviewers consistently praise friendly staff, including a manager who quickly handled a guest finding their reserved seat left messy by earlier occupants. D-Box motion seats with heaters and recline are called out as worth the upgrade. One detailed 2026 review requests unisex/universal restrooms and notes some auditorium wings sit underused outside peak hours.

locations.name: Studio Eats Colorado Springs
locations.description: Studio Eats concessions inside Cinemark Tinseltown Colorado Springs and XD. Google Place Details returned no textual reviews, so all service-model and amenity fields are ungraded.

locations.name: Movie Bistro - Fort Collins
locations.accessibility_notes: Reviewers ask for more visible row-letter markers.
locations.description: Cinemark's Movie Bistro in Fort Collins. Reviewers praise cleanliness, staff, and the food-and-beverage selection but rarely describe the service model itself; one useful complaint asks for clearer row-letter signage. Sparse text reviews overall, so seating type and in-theater service are ungraded.

locations.name: Studio Eats Kitchen & Bar - Manchester Buckland Hills
locations.description: Kitchen-and-bar attached to Cinemark Buckland Hills 18. Reviewers describe it as a quick sports-bar-style stop before a movie — burgers with fries, flatbreads, wings, and well-mixed drinks from an attentive bartender. Recent reports are mixed on food quality and note limited hours (closed weekdays, opens 3:30 PM weekends per one 2025 review) that cost the location some business.

locations.name: Studio Eats Kitchen & Bar - Milford
locations.description: Cinemark's Studio Eats Kitchen & Bar at Connecticut Post in Milford. Google Place Details returned no textual reviews, so all service-model and amenity fields are ungraded.

locations.name: Movie Bistro - Boca Raton
locations.description: Cinemark Bistro Boca Raton, with a long-running upstairs bistro reviewers describe as full table service to your seat — flatbreads, chicken nachos, Korean fried chicken pizza, and a rotating wine list (Whitehaven, formerly Kim Crawford) delivered during the film. Bartenders are called out by name (Linda, Shannon). Reviewers note that not every showtime is upstairs-bistro-eligible, and one 2025 review reported a ceiling leak from an upstairs urinal that ruined a Father's Day showing.

locations.name: The Premier - Boynton Beach
locations.safety_notes: One 2025 review reports a weekend policy that turned an adult sibling away when trying to buy tickets for underage siblings without a parent present.
locations.description: Concessions at Cinemark Boynton Beach 14 and XD; despite its listing under the /restaurants directory, reviewers describe a standard theater with rocker seating (not recliners, per an explicit reviewer note) and traditional popcorn/candy concessions rather than a full-service dining concept. One 2025 review documents a strict weekend policy requiring a parent or legal guardian for minors that turned an older sibling away at the counter.

locations.name: Studio Eats Jacksonville
locations.description: Studio Eats concessions inside Cinemark Jacksonville Atlantic North XD and ScreenX, with a game room on site. Reviewers describe in-seat drink and snack delivery — one specifically valued it for making the visit easier with two elderly companions. Cleanliness and the large XD screen draw consistent praise; a recurring complaint is restroom upkeep (low water pressure, empty soap dispensers, general griminess) despite the rest of the venue being well kept.

locations.name: Studio Eats Tinseltown Jacksonville
locations.description: Studio Eats concessions inside Cinemark Tinseltown Jacksonville and XD. Reviewers consistently praise cleanliness, comfortable custom recliners with adjustable footrests, and a smooth online ticket-and-food-ordering flow that has orders ready on arrival with no lines. Also hosts limited-run event screenings (a concert film cited by one reviewer). No complaints of substance found in the current review sample.

locations.name: Studio Eats Orlando
locations.description: Studio Eats concessions inside Cinemark Orlando and XD, which also offers private theater rentals for events (a birthday screening reviewer confirmed a well-stocked bar and staff willingness to restart a film for late arrivals). Reviewers consistently praise comfortable, quiet reclining seats and cleanliness, though the most recent reviews flag slow concession service during a Friday peak (30-minute wait, only 2 of 9 registers staffed) and some smell/cleanliness complaints near the soda station.

locations.name: Universal Cinemark at CityWalk
locations.parking_notes: On-site parking runs about $35; reviewers warn you need both copies of your parking receipt for validation at the counter.
locations.description: Universal Cinemark at Universal CityWalk Orlando — a large two-story, tourist-district theater rather than a Studio Eats/Reserve branded concept. Reviewers consistently praise comfortable electric reclining seats with swivel food/drink trays, cleanliness, and upstairs/downstairs concession stands. Recurring minor complaints: paid on-site parking ($35) requires keeping both ticket copies for validation, sticky/uncleaned condiment counters, and restrooms positioned far from some auditoriums.

locations.name: Studio Eats Durbin Park
locations.description: Food-and-beverage program inside Cinemark Durbin Park XD and ScreenX, with reviewers praising cleanliness and staff. Reclining, heated seats with pull-out side tables; a D-Box motion-seat auditorium is available as an upcharge. Concessions are described as varied but conventional (popcorn, drinks, snacks) — one reviewer flagged the use of canola oil for popcorn. Complaints center on inconsistent participation in advertised fan-event giveaways.

locations.name: Studio Eats Melrose Park
locations.description: Studio Eats concessions inside Cinemark Melrose Park and XD. Recent reviewers say a menu redesign shrank portions — 'cheese fries' called out as a third of their former size by a 20-year regular. Screens and sound get praise; recent front-of-house complaints center on staff attitude, seat wear (torn upholstery reported), and a locked-doors incident before a 10:30 AM showtime.

locations.name: Studio Eats Merriam
locations.description: Studio Eats concessions inside Cinemark Merriam and XD. Recent reviewers uniformly praise clean facilities, friendly counter staff, heated seats, and late showtimes; pricing is called out as a strength. No reviewer describes an in-seat food delivery service here.

locations.name: The Premier - Florence
locations.accessibility_notes: Reviewer notes a family bathroom on site.
locations.parking_notes: Reviewer notes plenty of free parking.
locations.safety_notes: A recent reviewer reported a broken recliner in Theater 5, Row H — worth flagging with staff before the show.
locations.description: Cinemark Florence 14 and XD, listed on Cinemark's /restaurants directory but described by reviewers as a standard theater with a bar area (frequently reported closed) and heavily upcharged concessions rather than a dining-forward venue. Luxury Loungers recline electronically with pull-out tray tables and heated seats — but recent reviews document broken recliners left in service and complain the 21+ VIP screens have been dropped. Reviewers do confirm the theater serves alcohol.

locations.name: Studio Eats Kitchen & Bar - Louisville Preston Crossings
locations.description: Studio Eats Kitchen & Bar inside Cinemark Preston Crossings 16 and XD. Reviews are sparse and older, with limited textual signal — a mid-movie sound outage and a general 'this place is good' comment among the most substantive. No reviewer describes the in-theater service model or bar clearly enough to grade.

locations.name: Studio Eats Louisville
locations.description: Studio Eats concessions inside Cinemark Tinseltown Louisville and XD, with reclining seats, swing-out trays, a fully stocked concession stand, and an arcade. A standout review praises a staff member (Diane) who personally accommodated a showtime change and prepared food for a guest with a time-sensitive tire repair appointment. One recent review flagged unaddressed disruptive kids and uncleaned seat/floor debris despite requesting management assistance during the film.

locations.name: Movie Bistro - Lake Charles
locations.description: Cinemark Bistro Lake Charles, with reviewers describing reclining seats and app-based food ordering delivered to the seat during the film — food is called convenient rather than exceptional. A 2024 review complained the bar was closed on the visit ('can't really call it a Bistro if the bar is closed down, not the first time'), so bar operation appears inconsistent. Concessions are considered expensive for portion size.

locations.name: Reserve Kitchen & Bar - Towson
locations.description: Cinemark's Reserve Kitchen & Bar at Towson. The most detailed recent review describes the menu as Applebee's/Chili's-tier American food at a decent price with limited fresh options; another calls the bar service and DJ music underwhelming. Sparse review coverage overall; service model is not clearly described.

locations.name: Studio Eats  Southland Center
locations.description: Studio Eats concessions inside Cinemark Southland Center and XD, framed by reviewers as a clean, well-run neighborhood theater with recliners (specifically contrasted against the Toledo Cinemark, which reviewers say lacks them). A reviewer specifically praised a BYO-container policy for popcorn (butter still provided). Front-of-house consistently gets high marks; no reviewer describes an in-theater dining service beyond concessions.

locations.name: Studio Eats Gulfport
locations.description: Studio Eats concessions inside Cinemark Gulfport 16, an older theater updated with recliners, D-Box motion seats, and Real 3D. Reviewers note the raised armrests are family-friendly (easier to cuddle kids), but that D-Box seats specifically don't recline and one reviewer felt they weren't worth the upcharge. A recent 1-star review from a Movie Club member reported the policy on outside cups tightened without notice, driving them to cancel their membership.

locations.name: Movie Bistro - Asheville
locations.description: Cinemark Bistro at The Carolina Asheville. Reviewers describe spacious, adjustable/reclining seats, a broad snack and drink selection (pizza, popcorn, beer), and generally friendly staff. Recent 1-star reviews center on age-verification for R-rated films being enforced abruptly at the counter, with one interaction with a manager named 'Ace' called out as dismissive.

locations.name: Movie Bistro - Charlotte
locations.accessibility_notes: Recent reviewer specifically praised staff for accommodating a neurodivergent teen group with in-seat food delivery so nobody had to miss the film.
locations.parking_notes: Ample free parking noted by reviewers; senior discount available at the box office.
locations.description: Cinemark Bistro Charlotte, recently upgraded with heated reclining chairs, alcoholic beverages, and — per multiple 2025 reviewers — a new in-seat food delivery service that has strained the concessions line to the point where reviewers say you need to arrive 30 minutes early. One reviewer explicitly recommends staying by the pickup door rather than returning to your seat while food is being prepared. A community group leader specifically praised the staff for accommodating a group of neurodivergent teens with in-seat delivery. Persistent low-level hissing sound in some auditoriums reported over the past year.

locations.name: Movie Bistro - Raleigh
locations.description: Cinemark Bistro Raleigh. Reviewers consistently praise reclining leather seats with side tables, tray tables (a specifically-called-out amenity), and friendly staff at both box office and concessions. A reviewer describes a chicken sandwich, cajun fries with 'slap sauce', chicken tenders, and garlic fries as standouts. The theater rents out private auditoriums for events (one reviewer attended a 'Stitching at the Movies' event). Recurring minor complaints: sound bleed between adjacent theaters and slow concession service at peak times.

locations.name: Studio Eats Rockingham Park
locations.description: Studio Eats concessions inside Cinemark Rockingham Park and XD. Reviewers highlight the XD widescreen paired with D-BOX motion seats — one flagged an important detail: the D-BOX functionality is tied to the specific seat you booked, so if someone else is in your seat, your motion doesn't work either. Reclining leather seats with three-level heated backs (cold/medium/hot). Concession selection is broad and food quality is well-reviewed. Bathrooms called out for needing more attention.

locations.name: Studio Eats Willowbrook Mall
locations.safety_notes: Recent reviewers flag persistent bathroom hygiene issues.
locations.description: Recently renovated into a dine-in theater at Cinemark Willowbrook Mall XD and ScreenX. Reviewers describe eat-on trays at every seat, D-BOX motion seats, and a 4DX auditorium — but the dine-in experience itself is called out as still catching up: a mid-2025 reviewer reported no way to order from an app or kiosk, no in-seat delivery available due to staffing, and a buzzer-based pickup system that pulls you out of the film. Recent hygiene complaints (bathrooms, seat area) are frequent.

locations.name: Studio Eats Kitchen & Bar - Beavercreek
locations.description: Studio Eats Kitchen & Bar at The Greene in Beavercreek. Reviewers describe a bartender-run ordering process with no printed menus — you decide from what's visible at the concession/bar area and order directly from the bartender. A game room is available for kids. Reviews are sparse and older overall; the most recent (2025) is a low-effort 2-star complaint about food quality with no specifics, alongside earlier positive reviews calling the seats and food good.

locations.name: Studio Eats Milford
locations.parking_notes: Ample free parking noted repeatedly by reviewers.
locations.description: Studio Eats concessions inside Cinemark Milford 16 (Ohio). Reviewers describe an older, unrenovated theater — one explicitly noted it hasn't been updated since construction and lacks recliners, and speculated an upgrade might not pencil out. Ample free parking. Staff consistently praised as friendly. Solid concession variety at average pricing; front-of-house sound issues in a Chainsaw Man screening flagged by one reviewer.

locations.name: Movie Bistro - North Canton
locations.description: Cinemark Bistro North Canton, described by reviewers as smaller and more intimate than the nearby Tinseltown (roughly a quarter the auditorium size). Servers bring food and alcoholic drinks to your seat during the film. Seats are XD lounger chairs with rotating trays that hold a large popcorn and drink; one reviewer specifically flagged that these loungers don't recline all the way — likely a safety limit tied to the in-seat dining. The Cinemark Movie Club membership is called out as paying for itself for regulars. Kettle corn (rare in the area) noted as a signature.

locations.name: Studio Eats Kitchen & Bar - Toledo Franklin Park
locations.description: Studio Eats Kitchen & Bar inside Cinemark Franklin Park 16 in Toledo. Google Place Details returned no textual reviews, so all service-model and amenity fields are ungraded. Note: a Southland Center reviewer explicitly contrasted the two, saying Toledo does not have recliners, which if accurate would explain the sparse recent traffic.

locations.name: Studio Eats Valley View
locations.safety_notes: A small number of reviewers over the years — including one within the last few months, with photo evidence — have reported seeing rodents in an auditorium. Rare relative to the location's overall review volume and strongly positive reputation, but worth knowing.
locations.description: Studio Eats concessions inside Cinemark Valley View XD and IMAX (Cleveland area). Recliner lounge chairs, XD and IMAX auditoriums, and an arcade (preloaded card required). Reviewers consistently praise cleanliness, staff, and comfort.

locations.name: Studio Eats  Dayton South
locations.description: Studio Eats concessions inside Cinemark Dayton South 16 and XD. Reviewers highlight comfortable seating and a well-liked door greeter ('Bodacious' called out by name), with recent complaints centering on inconsistent refill policies at concessions (large popcorn vs x-large, Icees vs fountain drinks) that reviewers say aren't clearly signposted. Auditorium and lobby cleanliness is generally solid.

locations.name: Studio Eats Tulsa
locations.description: Studio Eats concessions inside Cinemark Tulsa and IMAX. Reviewers describe leather reclining seats with three-level heated backs, a fair-sized arcade, and both concessions and alcoholic beverages available. Recent standout compliment for a manager who handled a disruptive-patron complaint with a refund and free ticket; recurring recent complaint is IMAX audio calibrated uncomfortably loud (multiple reviewers left mid-film covering their ears).

locations.name: Studio Eats Erie
locations.description: Studio Eats concessions inside Cinemark Tinseltown Erie, with a dedicated alcohol counter (staff member Gavin specifically praised for going out of his way to help locate a guest's lost keys). Most seats recline and reviewers describe near-private showings possible at early showtimes. A D-Box auditorium exists but one reviewer felt it wasn't worth the price, describing the room as uncomfortably warm. A 2025 review reported a sold-out popcorn-bucket promotion with no backup plan and a notably dirty women's restroom with visible empty liquor bottles left inside.

locations.name: Studio Eats Montage Mountain
locations.description: Studio Eats concessions inside Cinemark Montage Mountain 20 and XD in Moosic, PA. All auditoriums are luxury seating with assigned reserved seating. Reviewers frequently call out extensive concessions with self-serve extra butter, private theater and party-room rentals for events (staff members Nicole and LaShaun mentioned by name in the most detailed event review), and classic-movie throwback programming. Arcade area exists but its status is inconsistent per one reviewer.

locations.name: Studio Eats College Station
locations.description: Studio Eats concessions inside Cinemark College Station and XD. Reviewers describe all-reclining seating, a Cinemark Movie Club membership that waives online fees and gives 20% off concessions, and student ticket discounts. Outside snacks are reportedly allowed in. Recent minor complaint about rising beverage prices even with the member discount.

locations.name: The Kitchen at CUT! - Cypress
locations.description: CUT! by Cinemark Cypress, a full dine-in theater, kitchen, and bar concept with servers taking orders at your seat. Reviewers describe deep-reclining seat warmers, generous portions (kids' mac and cheese, brownie sundae delivered mid-film on request), and a full bar (margaritas specifically praised). Service quality is inconsistent across reviews — some report excellent, attentive staff by name (Aliya, David, Juan, Andrea) resolving seat and order issues promptly, while others report long waits for food/drinks (25-60+ minutes), billing for undelivered items, and dismissive management response during a busy Saturday. Restroom cleanliness flagged as a recurring weak point.

locations.name: Studio Eats Dallas
locations.description: Studio Eats concessions inside Cinemark Dallas XD and IMAX, home to a 70mm IMAX auditorium reviewers describe as visually stunning but with tight leg room and less-comfortable seats than other Cinemark locations. Cleanliness and staff friendliness get consistent praise. One detailed complaint alleges a cashier overcharged for a small order and pocketed the difference; a separate reviewer flagged seeing young children in an 18+ screening and wished staff enforced age policy more proactively.

locations.name: Movie Bistro - Edinburg
locations.description: Cinemark Bistro Edinburg. Reviewers describe standard (non-reclining, 'rocking chair'-style per one reviewer) seating, a Cinemark Movie Club membership providing 20% off, and food that must be ordered via app only at ticket purchase or otherwise from the counter — no full in-seat ordering flow. Items are sold à la carte with no combo pricing, unlike other Cinemark locations reviewers have visited. Food quality itself gets consistent praise; popcorn equipment cleanliness specifically noted as better-kept than competitors.

locations.name: Gamescape by Cinemark at El Paso
locations.description: Gamescape by Cinemark at El Paso — a bowling, arcade, and dining venue distinct from a standard in-theater dining concept, with reviewers describing bowling lanes with adjustable play settings, an arcade (called pricier than Dave & Buster's by one reviewer), and a food menu (chicken tenders, brisket nachos, chicken wraps) served at generous portions. Service is inconsistent per reviews — some report attentive named staff (Abraham, Avery), others describe a server who disappeared mid-order. Not an in-theater dine-in format; food and movie-going appear to be separate activities on site.

locations.name: Studio Eats Las Palmas
locations.description: Studio Eats concessions inside Cinemark Tinseltown Las Palmas XD and SCREENX. Reviewers describe satellite mini concession stands positioned near auditoriums that speed up refill lines, praised as a strong operational choice — but a separate 2025 review reports the opposite experience, with long main-line waits and unclear signage about the satellite stands' availability during a specific bad night, suggesting inconsistent staffing/execution rather than a structural amenity gap. A 2025 review also reports a broken A/C in one auditorium with staff offering only a refund/voucher rather than a fix.

locations.name: The Kitchen at CUT! - Frisco
locations.accessibility_notes: A reviewer notes staff accommodated a pregnancy-related seating request using an available disability seat.
locations.description: CUT! by Cinemark Frisco, a full dine-in theater, kitchen, and bar concept with table service to your seat. Reviewers describe good sound and comfortable seats when service goes well, and specifically praise staff flexibility around accessibility (one pregnant reviewer was seated in an unused disability seat without pushback). Recent reviews document a decline in food quality and consistency — repeatedly reheated/microwaved fries, wrong orders, and one incident where a server spilled a drink on a guest with no apology or comp. Order via the app is reportedly unreliable, often requiring an in-person server order instead.

locations.name: Studio Eats Kitchen - Grapevine
locations.accessibility_notes: A reviewer using a cane reports staff proactively offered elevator access to and from her seat.
locations.safety_notes: Multiple reviewers note the building has only one restroom for the entire multi-auditorium theater, located at the front of the building.
locations.description: Studio Eats concessions inside Cinemark Tinseltown Grapevine and XD. Seats include a heated, table-attached recliner option and D-Box motion seating, both well-reviewed. A specific accessibility note: a reviewer using a cane was offered elevator assistance to and from her seat by an assistant manager without being asked. A structural complaint recurs across reviews — the entire multi-auditorium building has only one restroom, located at the front of the building. Customer-service quality is inconsistent, with both strongly positive and strongly negative staff-interaction reports in the same review window.

locations.name: Gamescape by Cinemark at Greenville
locations.description: Gamescape by Cinemark at Greenville. Google Place Details returned no textual reviews, so all service-model and amenity fields are ungraded. Assumed to mirror the bowling/arcade/dining format of the El Paso Gamescape location pending direct evidence.

locations.name: Studio Eats Harlingen
locations.description: Studio Eats concessions inside Cinemark Harlingen 16 and XD. Reviewers consistently describe clean auditoriums, but recent reviews are dominated by concession-line and food-timing complaints — only the main concession stand is opened even during peak Tuesday crowds, with waits over 30 minutes leading to melted drinks and cold popcorn. A December 2025 review reports a showing cancelled after guests had already been seated for an hour, with no apology or refund and only rain-check passes offered. One reviewer specifically praised staff flexibility after a car accident caused a late arrival.

locations.name: Studio Eats Houston
locations.parking_notes: Reviewer notes a very large parking lot.
locations.description: Studio Eats concessions inside Cinemark Tinseltown Houston 290 and XD, with a margarita counter (ID-checked per a reviewer), a Pizza Hut counter, a large arcade with air hockey, and a fully stocked bar. Reviewers consistently praise friendly, attentive staff (Assistant Manager Javan specifically called out for helping carry concessions) and note the Cinemark Movie Club gives 20% off concessions with monthly rollover tickets. Recliners in the XD auditorium don't fully recline per one detailed review. A same-day online food-order pickup ran 25 minutes late for one reviewer, and staff declined to deliver it to the seat once the film had started.

locations.name: Studio Eats Katy
locations.description: Studio Eats concessions inside Cinemark Katy and XD, which also hosts a Pizza Hut counter. Reviewers describe comfortable recliners, clean bathrooms, and a wide concession/bar selection with helpful staff. One recurring minor complaint: advertised promotions (bonus popcorn buckets, plushie bundles) not always honored consistently at the register.

locations.name: Studio Eats Missouri City
locations.parking_notes: Reviewer notes a well-lit, well-patrolled parking lot with visible security.
locations.description: Studio Eats concessions inside Cinemark Missouri City and XD, offering in-seat food delivery. Reviewers repeatedly praise a specific manager (Joseph) for resolving order mix-ups and last-minute seating changes with genuine hospitality; a separate review documents strong event/birthday-party service from staff named Marcus, Melany, Jonathan, and Amarisse. Recurring complaint: evening service (post-sunset) runs into stock-outs and communication gaps between servers about what's in the kitchen, leading to delayed or incomplete orders. Parking lot has visible security, and door staff check ID for underage patrons.

locations.name: Reserve Kitchen & Bar - West Plano
locations.description: Cinemark's Reserve Kitchen & Bar at West Plano, described by regular customers as consistently good food and service on most visits, ordered for pickup or in-theater. Two standout negative reviews (four years apart) describe individual staff members being rude to customers over small requests (a glass of water, extra butter) — isolated incidents against an otherwise positive review pattern rather than a systemic issue.

locations.name: Studio Eats Kitchen & Bar - Legacy
locations.safety_notes: Multiple recent reviewers report the auditorium air conditioning failing with no staff response despite repeated in-person complaints.
locations.description: Studio Eats Kitchen & Bar inside Cinemark Legacy and XD, a large 20+ screen theater with party rooms and a small bistro seating area near the lobby. Reviewers describe slightly reclining seats (legs raise, seat doesn't table-tray) and a bar limited to beer, wine, margaritas, and one liquor mix. Food (pretzel bites, loaded nachos, mozzarella sticks) draws praise. Recurring complaints: no seat trays for food/drinks, and multiple recent reviews report the auditorium air conditioning failing with no staff response despite repeated complaints.

locations.name: Studio Eats The Woodlands
locations.parking_notes: Reviewer notes ample parking but says it can take a while to find a spot during busy times.
locations.description: Studio Eats concessions inside Cinemark The Woodlands and XD. Reviewers describe counter pickup with a no-wait, walk-up-and-grab model for online orders, reclining seats, and consistently friendly, name-recognized staff (Presley among those called out). Pricing favorably compared to Regal by one reviewer (~$12 vs ~$30 for an evening showtime). Theater temperature runs cold; multiple reviewers recommend bringing a layer.

locations.name: Studio Eats Waco
locations.safety_notes: A few recent reviewers report moths in multiple auditoriums.
locations.description: Studio Eats concessions inside Cinemark Waco and XD, with a D-Box auditorium reviewers specifically call out as a step up from other Waco theaters. Cleanliness and staff friendliness draw consistent praise, including a specific shoutout to a manager (Steven) who resolved an online ticketing error. One recurring complaint: moths flying in multiple auditoriums, occasionally distracting near the screen/projector.

locations.name: Studio Eats NASA
locations.parking_notes: Reviewer notes plenty of parking for a busy location.
locations.safety_notes: A 2025 reviewer reported a rat sighting near a seat several months prior; management responded with free passes and pest control, and the reviewer's follow-up visit found the theater clean.
locations.description: Studio Eats concessions inside Cinemark NASA and XD, home to a Pizza Hut counter. Reviewers describe recently upgraded reclining seats and enhanced sound. One detailed 2025 review reports a rat sighting near a seat months ago that management addressed with free passes and pest control, and confirms a follow-up visit found the theater clean and pest-free — useful context that the operator responded to and appears to have resolved the issue.

locations.name: Studio Eats Riverton
locations.description: Studio Eats concessions inside Cinemark Riverton and XD, in the Mountain View open-air mall. Reviewers consistently praise cleanliness, full recliner seating with seat warmers, and attentive staff (Brooke and Lydia specifically called out for handling a large group-ticket refund smoothly). No reviewer describes in-seat food delivery — concessions are counter pickup with pre-order/pickup for large popcorn orders.

locations.name: Studio Eats  Jordan Landing
locations.description: Studio Eats concessions inside Cinemark Jordan Landing 24 and XD, open since 1999 and reviewers specifically praise the theater for preserving its original character (classic movie photos lining the hallways) while modernizing ticket/concession flow. One reviewer describes food delivered to seats after ordering. Recurring complaints: the theater consistently runs warm, and a 2026 review reports worn/torn seat upholstery and uncleaned popcorn debris between showings, plus obstructive wall dividers between rows that block sightlines for shorter viewers.

locations.name: Studio Eats Kitchen & Bar - Fairfax
locations.description: Studio Eats Kitchen & Bar inside a Cinemark in Fairfax, VA. Review coverage is minimal and dated (most recent substantive review is 4 years old, praising staff friendliness); no reviewer describes the service model, seating, or bar clearly enough to grade.

locations.name: Reserve Restaurant & Bar | Pizzeria
locations.description: Full-service restaurant, bar, and pizzeria attached to a Cinemark theater in Newport News, connected to Paragon Theaters per one older review and previously operating under the names 'Neo Kitchen and Bar' and 'MiPie' before rebranding. Reviews span many years and are consistently rough on service — confused or absent host greetings, servers overheard shorting drink pours, and reports of being ignored at the bar for 10+ minutes while staff chatted among themselves. A positive minority describes a warm, attentive team and a well-regarded burger. A 2025 review notes the pizza recipe changed for the worse after the MiPie-to-Reserve transition.

locations.name: Reserve Kitchen & Bar - Bellevue Lincoln Square
locations.description: Cinemark's Reserve Kitchen & Bar at Lincoln Square in Bellevue. Review coverage is extremely sparse — a single detailed 1-star review describes staff rudely telling a group to move after another customer complained about their conversation volume; the remaining reviews carry no text. Not enough reviewer signal to grade the dining service model or amenities.
